Is Netflix a Buy for $1,000?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sizable down cycles aren't new to the Netflix (NFLX +1.32%) story.
  • History claims that the streaming stock has always made a comeback.
  • Is it time to buy Netflix for $1,000?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:10PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Sizable down cycles aren't new to the Netflix (NFLX +1.32%) story. The latest dip, with shares down 56% from their peak (as of Nov. 23), is certainly troubling for investors to witness. But it's smaller than the 76% drop in 2022 and the 79% fall before that in 2011.

History claims that the streaming stock has always made a comeback. And despite the most recent tumble, the shares have still returned 392% in the past 10 years. Getting in early on a true disruptor usually produces this type of performance.

Is it time to buy Netflix for $1,000? At the current price of $58.10, investors can add about 17 shares to their portfolios.

Netflix's economic moat comes from its scale. With more than 325 million paid memberships, it spreads its content budget across a far bigger audience than any rival can. That's a powerful cost advantage. Netflix is targeting a 31.5% operating margin in 2026. Walt Disney's (DIS +1.86%) non-sports streaming segment, which includes Disney+ and Hulu, posted an 11.5% margin in its latest fiscal year.

And the runway is still long if you ask the leadership team. Chief Financial Officer Spence Neumann mentioned in July that Netflix was "under 45% penetrated into addressable households around the world." It also captures 5% of TV viewing time and only about 7% of its addressable revenue opportunity.

The bottom line keeps improving. Operating margin expanded from 26.7% in 2024 to 29.5% in 2025 and is projected at 31.5% this year, as noted. Free cash flow is also expected to reach roughly $12 billion in 2026, compared to $9.5 billion last year. Growth is translating into serious profits.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

So why has Netflix stock gotten clobbered? Growth is slowing. Revenue increased 16.2% year over year in Q1 2026, 13.4% in Q2, and 11.8% in Q3. Wall Street expects 11.6% in the fourth quarter.

Engagement is a worry, too. View hours rose only 2% in the first half of 2026. Investors also didn't like management's decision to report that figure once a year, starting in 2027, instead of twice.

But all this pessimism has reset the valuation. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is now 15.1. That's cheaper than the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.50%). Shareholders aren't used to seeing Netflix shares on the discount rack.

Industry observers note that at this multiple, Netflix looks like an interesting buy with $1,000. Just don't expect a smooth ride. The stock could move with heightened volatility in the near term. That's why patience is critical.

#188287. Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it's not the point of the video, I know.
  • In a recent development, what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of New York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass.
  • That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's not the point of the video, I know. The clip the Fresh York Knicks posted late Sunday night was intended to celebrate Josh Hart producing arguably his best performance in what's been a rocky start to the season — 10 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a steal, his 18th triple-double in a Knicks uniform, tied for the second-most in franchise history — in a 113-106 win over the rival Indiana Pacers at Madison Square Garden.

In a recent development, what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of New York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass. And at the very start of the clip, before the camera pans over to Hart, there's only one Knicks player in sight: Karl-Anthony Towns.

That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.

The early-season MVP conversation pretty much starts and ends with Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić, the scoreboard-breaking titans leading the top two squads in the Western Conference. Expand the parameters out a little bit, though, and Towns — whose contract Knicks owner James L. Dolan declined to extend before the start of the season, and man, does it sure seem like the price is going up with every passing game — is forcing his way into the tier below them.

Sources indicate that the Knicks are, and always will be, Jalen Brunson's team. Through the first month of the 2026-27 NBA season, though — and, really, since the start of last postseason — you can make a legitimate case that Towns has been their best all-around player. And, if you're feeling spicy, maybe the best player in the entire conference.

Recent findings suggest that that's debatable, of course. Reasonable people can forward a number of names: Giannis Antetokounmpo, off to a scorching start to his tenure in South Beach; Cade Cunningham, still the straw that stirs the drink in Detroit; Tyrese Maxey, who's been the best player on the conference's No. 1 seed in Philly; Jayson Tatum, who had Boston off to a roaring start before some slippage out West.

Dig into the numbers, though, and Towns — the two-way heartbeat of a team that has won 11 of its past 14 games since an 0-3 start to move into a tie for second place in the East, boasting the NBA's third-best net rating in that span — has as good a case as any of them.

Recent findings suggest that entering Tuesday's action, Towns ranks third in the NBA in ESPN's net points per 100 possessions, behind only Wembanyama and Dončić. He's fourth in win shares, behind only Wembanyama, Dončić and Houston Rockets center Alperen Şengün. He's fifth in The BBall Index's LEBRON and box plus-minus, and sixth in win shares per 48 minutes, value over replacement player, Neil Paine's wins above replacement and Mike Beuoy's win probability added. He's seventh in player efficiency rating, ninth in DARKO daily plus-minus and tied for 10th among healthy players in Jeremias Engelmann's xRAPM. Which is to say: Take your pick of impact metrics, and KAT's right near the top, rubbing shoulders with the best of the best.

It has been revealed that maybe you're not such a significant fan of the all-in-one alphabet-soup metrics; maybe you like your numbers a little less advanced. Well, how's this:.

Towns enters Wednesday's 2026 Emirates NBA Cup meeting with the rival Cleveland Cavaliers averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. That makes him one of only three players in the NBA this season averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes a night, alongside Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić. He's hitting those numbers more efficiently than ever, too, shooting 61% on 2-pointers and 42% from long distance, scoring under 1.32 points per shot attempt with a .650 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both career highs.

(Bruno Rouby/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

Scoring plus rebounding plus playmaking plus efficiency is a pretty damn good combination. Prior to this season, Stathead's database lists only two players who've ever averaged more than 20 points per game, grabbed more than 20% of available rebounds, dished assists on more than 20% of his teammates' baskets, and posted a true shooting percentage north of .600: Giannis, back in 2019-20, and Jokić, who did it in 2021-22, '22-23 and '25-26.

Recent findings suggest that those seasons resulted in two MVP trophies and two runner-up finishes. That's the tech giant that KAT's keeping this season.

It has been revealed that (For the record: Wemby and Giannis are also keeping that company this season. Whew.).

According to recent reports, much of this stellar start goes back to those five principles — pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass — that Brown's been hammering ever since he got to New York. Towns might not be the first person you think of when you hear the word "pace," and the Knicks probably wouldn't be the first team to come to mind: They rank dead last in the NBA in number of possessions per 48 minutes, and tied for 28th in the average length of their offensive possessions. (Much, at times, to Brown's chagrin.) But while nobody will confuse Brown's charges for the Seven Seconds or Less Suns, they do move more swiftly with the 7-footer involved: The Knicks' average offensive possession is 1.3 seconds faster with Towns on the floor than off it — the largest differential of any Knick who's played actual minutes.

According to recent reports, "Space," obviously, is a little easier to square here. Long heralded as perhaps the sweetest-shooting big man of all time (including, um, by himself), Towns is attempting eight 3-pointers per 100 possessions this season, the most since his last season in Minnesota and the fourth-most of his career. He boasts the third-highest average gravity of any center — an NBA Advanced Stats metric aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — behind only Wembanyama and Joel Embiid. (Towns also outpaces both in perimeter gravity when he's off the ball, meaning he's drawing more attention than either of them when he's spaced and doesn't have possession — creating wider driving and passing lanes for his teammates to exploit.).

In a recent development, when Towns does have the ball, he's wasting precious little time before attacking. Among 80 players averaging at least 50 touches per game this season, Towns averages the second-fewest dribbles per touch and has the seventh-lowest average touch time, holding on to the ball for just 1.8 seconds on average, according to Second Spectrum tracking data. He's one of 12 Knicks under two seconds per touch — evidence of widespread adherence to Brown's insistence on quick decision-making.

Recent findings suggest that when the substantial fella decides to move, he's often aimed at the lane. Despite spending a significant share of his floor time setting high ball screens, spacing the floor or facilitating from up top, Towns leads the Knicks in paint touches per game — he's 26th in the league in total paint touches — and is taking a career-high 53% of his shots at the rim this season.

Industry observers note that he's actually driving to the cup less frequently — just 5.5 dribble-drives per game this season, down from 8.1 last season and 11.3 in 2024-25. He's been an absolute monster on those forays to the basket, though, scoring nearly a point per drive and shooting 67% on those plays. He's finishing tough through the contact he draws in the lane, too: Nearly 35% of the shooting fouls he absorbs have ended in an and-one — also near a career-high.

Thanks partly to the pressure Towns puts on the rim himself, and partly to how his presence on the perimeter opens up the floor for his teammates, the Knicks take 34.5% of their field-goal attempts at the rim with him in the game — a near-top-five rate in the league, according to Cleaning the Glass. That rate drops to 25.8% when he's off the floor, which would sit just 26th in the NBA.

That just leaves "crash the glass" … which Towns is doing to the tune of hauling in a career-high 11.3% of available offensive rebounds. He's turning the garbage into gold, too, tied for sixth in the NBA in second-chance points per game — one major reason why Latest York ranks in the top five in putback scoring efficiency.

According to recent reports, when Brown took over, he made it clear exactly what he wanted his players to do — what he believed they had to do to reach the grandest goal in the game. After achieving it, he demanded nothing less. More than any other player in orange and blue, Towns has delivered it, night after night after night.

According to recent reports, "Ever since I got here, all I've ever remarked is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," Towns told reporters earlier this month. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team.".

It has been revealed that that's the funny thing about basketball, though. Sometimes, being willing to give it up means you wind up getting it back in an even better position to do something with it.

Recent findings suggest that the sacrifice-minded Towns' usage rate, average time of possession and field goal attempts per 100 possessions are all up a tick from last season. And with Upcoming York more frequently operating its offense through Towns as a playmaking hub at the top of the floor — a carryover from the success the Knicks found with those looks last postseason, which has helped unlock Brunson as an off-ball weapon and unleashed a devastating split-cut game — he's averaging 43.4 frontcourt touches per game this season, according to Second Spectrum tracking. That's the fifth-highest mark in the NBA this season, and KAT's heaviest half-court workload in five years.

According to recent reports, towns has been brilliant in that more central role, whether looking for his own opportunities or quarterbacking the offense to set the table for Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart and the rest of the defending champs. He has notched the assist on 21.9% of his teammates' baskets during his time on the court — a significant leap from his first two seasons as a Knick, and a near-top-10 mark among power forward/center types thus far this season.

Recent findings suggest that newly introduced York's live-ball turnover rate drops by eight percentage points in KAT's minutes, and its shooting efficiency improves by eight percentage points, according to PBP Stats. When he's on the floor, nearly 60% of the Knicks' 2-point field goals have come via assist — up from 50% when he's on the bench. That's the difference between top-three in the league and bottom-five.

"They've done a great job of making their offense multifaceted," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters when the Knicks visited — and beat — Minnesota last week. "They still have Brunson doing his thing. And now KAT, playing through him — we talked about how that was something that they found last year to go to late in the season, in the playoffs. And now, the Brunson-KAT two-man game is better than it's ever been.".

So, too, is Towns' work on the defensive end — so often maligned over the course of his 12-year career, but something that started to become a legitimate strength early last season, sustained at a high level through the Knicks' championship run, and has carried over to the start of this season.

As aggressively as Towns crashes the offensive glass, he has hit the boards even harder on the other end, leading the NBA in defensive rebounds and total rebounds per game. All that possession-finishing has led to him finishing all 16 games he's played this season with a double-double — the longest such streak to open a season by any Knicks player ever, and the fourth-longest season-starting streak by any player since the ABA-NBA merger, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes. KAT's company there, again: Jokić, Giannis … and prime Bill Walton.

Towns' defensive contributions extend beyond rebounding, though. He's become much more comfortable playing multiple defensive schemes, including more frequently playing up higher on the floor to take away ball-handlers' airspace in the pick-and-roll. He's been active and aggressive with his hands, posting the highest steal rate of his career and his highest block rate since 2021-22 — and, crucially, doing so without hacking, averaging his fewest personal fouls per 36 minutes since 2019-20.

Industry observers note that "KAT's got tremendous feel," Brown recently told reporters. "He's a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball.".

Industry observers note that and when he's sunk back into the paint in drop coverage, Towns has proved a sturdier interior deterrent than his reputation would suggest. The share of opponents' field goal attempts that come at the basket plummets with him in the game, and opponents are shooting 55.3% at the rim when he's the nearest defender, according to Second Spectrum tracking — that's 25th among 86 players who've defended at least 40 up-close attempts, and on pace to be the second-best mark of his career. All told, the Knicks are allowing just 106.3 points-per-100 in Towns' minutes — a level of defensive efficiency that would be No. 2 in the NBA, behind only his old pals in Minnesota.

In a recent development, so: What do you get when you combine a skeleton-key stretch major man who unlocks a championship-level offense with a defensive anchor capable of serving as the backstop of a top-five defense, all while playing major minutes at an elite level of offensive efficiency? It sure sounds like one of the best, most important — dare we say, most valuable? — players you can have in the modern NBA.

Maybe, in a world where Wemby and Luka and SGA exist, that all doesn't add up to an MVP trophy. It does, though, produce a player that's a hell of a lot closer to top-five in the world than he is to missing the All-NBA ballot — which Towns did last season (unjustly, in my view). And, if KAT and the Knicks can keep up the flow they've found since their slow start, it ought to produce one hell of a title defense.

By Jeff Siegel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:13PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

According to recent reports, coca-Cola (KO +1.81%) has increased its dividend for 64 consecutive years. In February 2026, the beverage giant raised its quarterly payout by roughly 4%, from $0.51 to $0.53 per share. That brings its annual dividend to $2.12 per share.

So what could a $10,000 investment in Coca-Cola generate in dividend income over the next decade?

At Coca-Cola's Nov. 20 closing price of $96.99, a $10,000 investment would purchase around 103.1 shares. With an annual dividend of $2.12 per share, those shares would generate approximately $219 in annual income today, representing a dividend yield of roughly 2.2%.

Industry observers note that but Coca-Cola has a long history of increasing its payout. Assuming the firm continues raising its dividend by 4% annually, its annual dividend could reach $3.14 per share by 2036. That would produce $324 in annual dividend income on the original investment, without purchasing additional shares. And over the entire decade, you would also collect around $2,600 in cumulative dividends.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

In a recent development, coca-Cola benefits from a portfolio of globally recognized beverage brands, including Sprite, Fanta, and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar. Its established distribution network, recurring consumer demand, and ability to raise prices help support consistent cash generation.

That said, the company faces challenges, including shifting consumer preferences, rising operating costs, and currency fluctuations. And while Coca-Cola's dividend history is impressive, future increases aren't guaranteed.

According to recent reports, I wouldn't expect Coca-Cola to deliver explosive growth. At nearly $97 per share, the stock isn't particularly cheap either. But if you're seeking dependable income, Coca-Cola remains an attractive long-term candidate.

My prediction is that a $10,000 investment today could generate approximately $324 in annual dividends by 2036, assuming 4% annual dividend growth and no reinvestment. That's a roughly 48% increase in annual income from the original investment, excluding any potential stock price appreciation. That's not bad.

    I gave Gemini access to my Wallet, and it immediately started saving me money

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, proposal a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.
    • Starting today, Google announced, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive.
    • Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, proposal a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

    Starting today, Google announced, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

    Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

    This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

    In a recent development, once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

    I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

    “You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response stated, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

    Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

    When I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

    Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Latest York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

    Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

    While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • It has been revealed that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    It has been revealed that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    According to recent reports, merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Sources indicate that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    According to recent reports, some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Industry observers note that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Industry observers note that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Recent findings suggest that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Recent findings suggest that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    Industry observers note that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    It has been revealed that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Sources indicate that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a substantial impact when you add several of them together.

    Industry observers note that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    Industry News: Retiring in 2027? Here's How Much Cash You Need to Set Aside

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that you'll often hear that it's important to continue investing during retirement.
    • You want your money to keep pace with inflation.
    • According to recent reports, at the same time, it's key to have some cash on hand in case the market doesn't perform well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:22PM EST.

    Recent findings suggest that you'll often hear that it's important to continue investing during retirement. And the reason is simple.

    You want your money to keep pace with inflation. If you pull your entire IRA or 401(k) out of the stock market and put it into cash, you might lose out on buying power through the years.

    According to recent reports, at the same time, it's key to have some cash on hand in case the market doesn't perform well. And if you're retiring in 2027, now's the time to secure that cash reserve before you start living off your portfolio.

    Recent findings suggest that the reason you need a pile of cash in retirement is simple. You never know what the stock market is going to do on any given day.

    According to recent reports, if you're at a point in life when you're using your portfolio for income, you may not have the luxury to wait months or years for a recovery. Your bills need to get paid now.

    If you set aside a cash reserve, you'll be able to leave your investments alone during a stock market downturn. That means instead of locking in permanent losses, you'll give your portfolio a chance to recover. If you don't keep some cash on hand and your bills can't wait, you could end up selling assets at a loss, increasing the risk of depleting your savings.

    According to recent reports, while it's notable to have some cash available in retirement, you don't want to go overboard. Keeping too much cash on hand could mean losing out on stronger returns.

    As a general rule of thumb, you may want to aim for one to three years' worth of living expenses in cash. That gives you time to ride out a prolonged market downturn. The exact amount you land on should hinge on how much peace of mind you want and what your spending and non-portfolio income sources look like.

    Sources indicate that if you're the type to lose sleep over a stock market crash, a three-year cushion may be best. On the other hand, if your budget is flexible, you have generous Social Security benefits coming your way, and you're open to working to supplement your income when needed, a one-year cash cushion may be enough.

    In a recent development, either way, if your retirement date is getting closer, start strategically moving assets into cash now. Decide on the amount you need, and shop around for a high-yield savings account so you can earn a decent return on your money.

    Recent findings suggest that you may also want to look at a CD ladder if you'll be setting aside a larger amount of cash, like two to three years' worth. If you set up those CDs to mature at regular intervals, you can retain access to your cash while potentially earning a higher return than a regular savings account.

    By Sarah Sidlow – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 5:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Kraft Heinz ›.

    Investors often weigh the safety of household staples against the excitement of growth brands. Let's see if Kraft Heinz (KHC +1.87%) or On (ONON +1.58%) is the better buy for your portfolio.

    Kraft Heinz operates as a global food giant with iconic household brands, while On is a Swiss athletic brand disrupting the footwear market. While they serve different consumer needs, both companies are vying for space in diversified portfolios, making them an interesting pair to compare for long-term growth and stability.

    According to recent reports, the company focuses on its North America Retail and International Developed Markets segments, moving brands like Heinz and Philadelphia through a vast distribution network. Walmart (WMT +2.11%) is the largest customer, representing nearly 21% of net sales, and customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business. Kraft Heinz also provides products for many foodservice distributors, reaching consumers in restaurants and on the go.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached nearly $24.8 billion, representing a decrease of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior year. The company reported a net loss of close to $3.5 billion during this same period. This decline in revenue suggests a challenging environment for top-line growth as consumer spending patterns shift.

    The debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.5x as of its December 2025 balance sheet. This ratio measures total debt against shareholder equity, where a lower number indicates less reliance on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures a tech giant's ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets, was approximately 1.2x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.7 billion.

    It has been revealed that on focuses on a premium performance strategy, selling high-end running shoes and apparel through a mix of wholesale partners and its own retail stores. The brand has expanded rapidly across the Americas and Asia-Pacific, relying on a premium image to attract athletes and lifestyle consumers alike. By controlling its direct-to-consumer channels, the manufacturer maintains higher oversight of its brand presentation and customer relationships.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $4.0 billion, a significant increase of roughly 17.4% year over year. Net income for this period was close to $527.4 million. This strong growth in both revenue and net income highlights the brand's momentum in the global footwear and apparel market.

    Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.4x, indicating that the tech giant has a conservative amount of debt relative to its equity. The current ratio was approximately 2.7x, suggesting a robust ability to cover its immediate financial liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $301.8 million.

    Recent findings suggest that kraft Heinz faces significant risks from its dependence on large retail customers like Walmart, which can exert pricing pressure. The manufacturer also faces competition from other packaged food giants like J. M. Smucker (SJM -1.45%) as private-label brands gain market share. Additionally, failure to adapt to shifting consumer health preferences or volatility in commodity prices for meat and dairy can negatively impact profitability.

    On must navigate intense competition in the premium footwear market from large established players. As a brand that relies on a premium reputation, any failure to maintain its brand image or keep pace with technological innovations could harm its growth. Additionally, expansion into newly introduced international markets carries execution risks, including varying consumer tastes and complex supply chain logistics.

    Kraft Heinz appears to be more conservatively valued based on its Forward P/E, while On carries a higher P/S ratio relative to sales over the past 12 months.

    According to recent reports, kraft Heinz has been a stalwart on the stock market and store shelves for decades, and its ubiquity in both areas is part of its appeal.     But Kraft Heinz also offers something On can't: Its products are inexpensive consumer staples, and in uncertain economic conditions, packaged foods products have historically held up well. It's arguably easier to forgo expensive running shoes than the staples for at-home meals.

    Industry observers note that fresh kid on the block On continues to grow revenue and net income. Its premium brand and direct-to-consumer business model has allowed it to maintain pricing power.     Breaking: Tidal to Reject and Remove Music That Is 100% AI

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The music streaming app announced on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated.
    • The app also noted distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.
    • Sources indicate that according to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app announced on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform said it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

    The app also noted distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

    Sources indicate that according to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal mentioned the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

    Industry observers note that before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app said it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

    Tidal said there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

    The organization has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

    Some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

    Tidal didn’t specify how much AI help would be allowed.

    A representative for Tidal didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

    Recent findings suggest that “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the manufacturer remarked in its announcement. “Everything in this upgrade comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

    Recent findings suggest that generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

    AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

    But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that youTube recently rolled out a fresh labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.

    Dreading Holiday Money Talks With Family? Here's What to Say

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.
    • Recent findings suggest that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial plans.
    • Industry observers note that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.

    Recent findings suggest that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial plans. That might involve asking you to lend money or your credit.

    Industry observers note that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out. But it’s crucial to establish boundaries so you don’t end up making a decision you’ll regret.

    According to recent reports, if you suspect a money request is coming your way, think carefully about what you’re willing — and able — to offer. You might choose a specific dollar limit or to give no financial help at all.

    In a recent development, “Only lend what you're truly OK losing,” says Alvin Carlos, a certified financial planner at District Capital Management in Washington, D.C. “Look at your budget and decide what you could hand over and never see again.”.

    Sources indicate that choose the language that best fits your situation. Adapt your responses as needed to guide the conversation in a direction that works for you.

    “I understand that you need help. I just need to review my own finances before I can give you an answer. I’ll get back to you by [day].”.

    If the request comes up at a holiday or family gathering:.

    “I’d rather discuss this privately. Let’s find another time to talk.”.

    “Here's what I’m comfortable with, and here's what I have to protect to be financially safe, mentally safe, and to continue to be there for you in the ways that you need me.”Or, if you want to be more direct:.

    Sometimes, there’s an unspoken expectation to give money because of how much loved ones think you earn, notes Ashley Agnew, a certified financial therapist in Boston.

    Getting ahead of it before there's a tipping point can help with tricky dynamics, she claims.

    According to recent reports, A recent Edward Jones report found that only about one-third of financial caregiving arrangements were planned and discussed in advance. The report also found that nearly half of financial caregivers (49%) make financial sacrifices, such as reducing or stopping saving, or tapping into their retirement account.

    Factor your financial health, your values and emotional well-being into your decision:.

    Review your income, expenses and savings. If you provide financial help and don’t get the money back, would you struggle to pay bills or reach financial goals? Prioritize building an emergency fund, saving for retirement and paying off high-interest debt first, Carlos says.

    Consider your relationship. Would you feel resentful if you aren’t repaid? How do you think your friend or relative would react if you decline to help? Could it damage your relationship, and if so, is it worth it?

    Understand the credit risks. Co-signing or allowing someone else to use your credit can leave you responsible for payments and expose you to potential credit damage.

    Know the tax implications. If you’re considering a substantial gift or loan, check with a tax professional about any reporting requirements and tax consequences.

    It has been revealed that consult your partner. If you share finances, make sure to include your partner in your decision-making process, Agnew says. If you have a parent asking for financial assistance, for example, but your cultural view is different from your spouse's, that’s a significant opportunity for a rift.

    Recent findings suggest that aim to be clear and direct. When in doubt, keep your answer concise, Agnew says.

    “Keeping it short and sweet will communicate that you've made a decision, not that you've requested a negotiation.”.

    Depending on where you left the conversation, you might have more steps to take.

    Stick to your boundaries and promises. Did you offer to contribute money? Pay as agreed. Did you say no? Don’t let your friend's or family member’s persistence, or the opinions of other friends and relatives, change your mind.

    If you offered to provide nonfinancial support, Carlos recommends pointing your loved one to local government and nonprofit resources. That might include emergency rent assistance, cheap or free financial advice, food banks and career services.

    Sources indicate that document the details and set the plan in motion. If you agreed to loan money, send your relative a quick text recapping the terms, Carlos claims. He also suggests setting up a simple repayment system together, such as a recurring Zelle or Venmo transfer.

    “Fewer reminders from you mean less tension,” he notes.

    According to recent reports, get outside help, if necessary. Despite your best efforts, it can be difficult to handle the situation on your own. If you’re feeling lingering stress or your family can’t reach a resolution, you might want to bring in some help, Agnew claims.

    She recommends working with a financial therapist or advisor, or using a financial wellness app.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:26PM EST.

    Cryptocurrency markets suffered another setback on Tuesday, November 24, as Bitcoin slipped below the psychologically important $60,000 level. Renewed weakness in technology stocks added to selling pressure, leaving major digital assets struggling to sustain their recent recovery.

    According to recent reports, as of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -3.27%) had fallen 2.44% to $59,718.51, while Ethereum (ETH -2.80%) declined 2.07% to $1,673.50. Solana (SOL -3.94%) suffered steeper losses, dropping 3.86% to $69.20.

    According to recent reports, deteriorating risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Tuesday as renewed selling across technology stocks and a strengthening U.S. dollar put additional pressure on digital assets. The reversal in Wall Street's recent rally has reinforced concerns about the cryptocurrency market's vulnerability to broader financial conditions, particularly as investors remain cautious about speculative assets.

    Institutional selling has compounded these challenges. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded approximately $4.71 billion in net outflows so far in November, marking their largest monthly withdrawal total on record. The persistence of these outflows has removed a significant source of buying demand, making it increasingly difficult for cryptocurrencies to sustain a recovery despite occasional rebounds in broader financial markets.

    Sources indicate that U.S.-listed cryptocurrency ETFs continued to decline on Tuesday, reflecting renewed selling pressure across digital asset markets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -2.48%) fell 2.48%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -2.35%) declined 2.35%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA -2.98%) dropped 2.98%.

    The cryptocurrency market's continued weakness highlights the growing disconnect between short-term price recoveries and underlying investor demand. Bitcoin's latest decline below $60,000, alongside renewed losses in Ethereum and Solana, suggests that recent rebounds have done little to reverse the broader bearish trend.

    Another concern is the accumulation of investors holding positions at substantially higher prices. As cryptocurrencies attempt to recover, investors looking to exit at smaller losses could introduce additional selling pressure. For Bitcoin, the $70,000 to $75,000 range may prove particularly challenging, while Ethereum and Solana face similar obstacles after breaking through notable price levels during the recent downturn.

    Looking ahead, the broader macroeconomic environment remains an important risk. Cryptocurrencies have struggled to participate in recent equity rallies but have remained vulnerable when technology stocks decline. Unless institutional capital flows stabilize and buying demand strengthens across major digital assets, further weakness in equities could accelerate cryptocurrency losses. Investors should look for sustained improvements in ETF flows, market liquidity, and firmer price trends before interpreting a temporary rebound as a lasting recovery.

    Mortgage Rates Today, Monday, November 23: Decidedly Higher

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.
    • In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • In a recent development, recently news about big tech has often pulled rates down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

    In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    In a recent development, recently news about big tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

    In a recent development, today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

    Here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    It has been revealed that lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of substantial tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

    The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

    Recent findings suggest that the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

    According to recent reports, we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three significant inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI revealed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Recent findings suggest that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    Sources indicate that P.S.: I don't have to ask if anyone's playing Grand Theft Auto 'cause c'mon, of course. But did anyone else perk up when Lu asked about home loans? Yeah, that was probably just me. Jason and Lucia would have to change a lot about their lifestyle to qualify (we know they're working on building credit, but having all your income be cash you can't really document is not going to work for a lender). But hey, I'm rooting for them.

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    It has been revealed that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    It has been revealed that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    According to recent reports, if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    Dick’s Sporting Goods Raised Its Full-Year Earnings Forecast as Foot Locker Returned to Positive Comparable Sales. Here's What Investors Need to Know.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Dick's Sporting Goods ›.
    • It has been revealed that A turnaround at a major operating unit, estimates-beating numbers, and a raise in profitability guidance powered Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS +14.59%) stock to a double-digit gain on Tuesday.
    • Here's a look at how Dick's did overall and whether investors can expect further gains from the veteran athletic-gear purveyor.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:31PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dick's Sporting Goods ›.

    It has been revealed that A turnaround at a major operating unit, estimates-beating numbers, and a raise in profitability guidance powered Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS +14.59%) stock to a double-digit gain on Tuesday. The specialty retailer's third quarter not only featured better-than-expected financials but also growth from the struggling brand it acquired last year.

    Here's a look at how Dick's did overall and whether investors can expect further gains from the veteran athletic-gear purveyor.

    In a recent development, dick's net sales in the quarter were $5.13 billion, 23% higher year over year. The caveat to this is the mentioned brand, Foot Locker, which the company acquired in 2025. That acquisition closed in early September of that year; as a result, only 8 weeks of Foot Locker's results were consolidated into Dick's third-quarter 2025 accounting -- hence the significant difference between last third quarter's sales and this one.

    It has been revealed that stripping Foot Locker out of the equation, the tech giant's comparable sales rose by 2.6% in the quarter. Dick's mentioned this was largely due to a rise in average ticket (i.e., average customer spending per transaction), offset by a slight decline in the number of transactions. On a pro forma basis, Foot Locker posted a 0.5% improvement. On a consolidated, pro forma basis for the company as a whole, comparable sales were 1.8% higher.

    According to recent reports, turning to profitability, non-GAAP (adjusted) net income came in at $167.5 million, or $1.94 per share. That was down from $180.6 million in the year-ago quarter.

    Despite the bottom-line slide, Dick's easily beat the consensus analyst estimates. Prognosticators tracking the company were modeling net sales of $5.08 billion, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of merely $1.42.

    It has been revealed that while those key fundamentals headed in an encouraging direction, it was Foot Locker's performance that really won the race for Dick's. That 0.5% increase in the brand's "comps" is quite an achievement -- it's the first time since the acquisition that it's been in the black.

    It has been revealed that previously, many investors had considered it to be a laggard. The unit didn't seem like a potential winner at all, with its 3.6% decrease in pro forma comps only one quarter ago.

    It still has some distance to run. In the conference call discussing the third-quarter results, management stated that Foot Locker performed particularly well in its core U.S. operating unit, which delivered comps of 4.1%. But the overall number was dragged down by sluggish performance in the Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) super-region. The brand was also burdened by high inventory levels, which required discounting to reduce.

    Another negative for Foot Locker is Nike's (NKE +5.89%) reset of its storied Jordan sneaker brand, which is aging and suffers from oversupply. Like any major brand overhaul, this will take some time -- Nike flagged fiscal 2029 for Jordan to return to growth. Nike footwear is a major draw within Foot Locker's product selection.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    It has been revealed that given that, Dick's maintained its guidance for full-year Foot Locker sales and comps. Specifically, it's expecting the unit to contribute $7.4 billion to $7.5 billion to the top line, with comparable sales expected to be flat to 2% down. Its operating loss should range from $40 million to $80 million.

    But the core Dick's business should compensate for this. Management raised the low end of the unit's net sales forecast from $14.5 billion to $14.6 billion, maintaining the high end of $14.7 billion. Ditto for comps, now expected to be 3.3% to 4% (previously 2.5% at the bottom end).

    All in all, the manufacturer is expecting a prosperous year. With the boosts to the Dick's unit estimates, the company's overall guidance is higher. The fresh floor for overall net sales is $22 billion (formerly $21.9 billion), with the maximum holding steady at $22.2 billion. Better, adjusted EPS is now anticipated to land at $11.45 to $12.30, up notably from the preceding forecast of $11 to $12.

    So, can we consider Dick's stock a buy candidate? I think much will depend on Foot Locker, which, given its size, has a significant impact on its parent's results. Despite investor excitement over the brand’s positive third-quarter comps figure, it still needs to improve sufficiently to become a regular, meaningful contributor to overall organization growth. It has to work through its inventory concerns and develop strategies to grow during the "Jordan gap.".

    Industry observers note that that stated, Dick's stock offers a high-yield dividend (currently paying 3.3%) that appears quite sustainable, and its core business is performing well. I also like the rather modest forward P/E of under 13. To me, these factors make the shares attractive, but more for those with a relatively long-term investment horizon.

    By Emma Newbery – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:36PM EST.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR -8.60%), an Ethereum (ETH -2.80%) treasury accumulation and Bitcoin (BTC -3.27%) ecosystem services provider, closed at $13.18, down 8.60%. Shares fell as the tech giant added to its ETH position and a broader crypto pullback hit treasury stocks.Trading volume reached 51.9 million shares, coming in about 44% above its three-month average of 36.1 million shares. Bitmine Immersion Technologies, which is primarily an Ethereum treasury manufacturer, has plummeted further: the stock has dropped 41% over the past month.

    Holding stock in crypto treasury companies is not the same as owning the digital assets directly or buying a crypto ETF. In the case of Bitmine, it set out to buy 5% of all the Ethereum in circulation and generate returns by staking its holdings. The firm has bought steadily through market turbulence, adding to its Ethereum holdings every week since June 2025 and now holds 4.98% of circulating ETH.

    According to recent reports, the difficulty for investors is that Ethereum’s price has fallen around 30% since the firm started its weekly purchases, and Bitmine is underwater on its holdings. I am optimistic about Ethereum in the long term -- as the biggest smart-contract crypto, it is well-positioned to benefit from any growth in the stablecoin and real-world asset tokenization markets. However, I am less optimistic about Bitmine because the treasury model carries too many risks, including share dilution, liquidation, and management changes. Ethereum ETFs allow investors to access Ethereum through their brokerage accounts and custody solutions, without the risks associated with treasury companies.

    I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.
    • By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.
    • In a recent development, I should have plenty of opportunities this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

    It’s a big list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

    By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

    In a recent development, I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) proposal to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL consumers expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

    Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

    Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

    Brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, notes many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

    Sources indicate that “They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

    Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

    According to recent reports, while Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

    But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

    “With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

    Sources indicate that not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

    In a recent development, there are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

    Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

    In a recent development, long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

    Industry observers note that pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

    According to recent reports, harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL company doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

    Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

    Sources indicate that because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

    According to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL users had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

    Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison says.

    Industry observers note that “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he says. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

    Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

    Recent findings suggest that still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison says, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

    Industry observers note that “Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he says. “There's a big difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.
