    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With Bitcoin (BTC -3.46%) collapsing below $60,000 on Nov.
    • 23, Jensen Huang's return as CEO lifted Nvidia's shares by 27%, but Bitcoin by only 0.6%, and the coin fell back beneath the $60,000 level within 24 hours anyway.
    • This isn't the first time that dynamic has reared its head, and it tends to make the idea of buying future dips a bit less attractive.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Alex Carchidi – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:41PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

    With Bitcoin (BTC -3.46%) collapsing below $60,000 on Nov. 20 to hit $55,081 the next day as the Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) drama continued, it's worth pondering whether this is a good opportunity to buy the dip, or if it's a trap for those who refuse to recognize that the market is turning against it.

    On Nov. 23, Jensen Huang's return as CEO lifted Nvidia's shares by 27%, but Bitcoin by only 0.6%, and the coin fell back beneath the $60,000 level within 24 hours anyway. In other words, it lost more during volatility that was mostly unrelated to it than it was able to regain once its trigger reversed.

    This isn't the first time that dynamic has reared its head, and it tends to make the idea of buying future dips a bit less attractive. Let's dive in and analyze the situation.

    The lopsided response that disfavors Bitcoin is somewhat attributable to who was selling it and the duration of their holding.

    It has been revealed that most of November's sellers had held their coins for under six months. Their losses, measured against past-year profits, reached levels seen only near the 2018, 2020, 2022, and early 2023 lows. Such capitulation, which is to say panicked bulk selling at a loss, often sends prices well below what the news actually justifies -- and in this case, Nvidia's problems are mostly distinct from Bitcoin's, but the justified fears of a potential incoming rate hike by the Federal Reserve are not.

    It has been revealed that nonetheless, dip buyers picked up about 66,000 BTC when it was priced between $62,000 and $66,000, only to see that price floor break within a week. Their losses may well be erased if they hold for the long term, but for now, they're underwater, which may make it stressful or unappealing for some investors to buy the slightly deeper dip this time around.

    Now let's hear the other side of the argument. The Nov. 21 low comes four years to the day after the coin's 2022 bear market bottom. If the four-year cyclical rhythm of Bitcoin continues, that timing favors buyers.

    According to recent reports, the next halving, which halves latest coin output, is due in April 2028. Bitcoin has historically bottomed out 12 to 18 months before a halving. That puts the window for the bottom between about October 2026 and April 2027, so those who buy the dip now could be well-positioned for that bull run, if it occurs.

    The market is obviously disfavoring the coin compared to other investments, and it has been doing so for a while. It only grew by 6% over the last five years. Its core investment thesis is still valid, but there could still be downside from here.

    Thus, I'm interested in buying some Bitcoin here, but only with a small amount of capital, and only because I know I'm willing to hold it for many years to come.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two latest credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    Recent findings suggest that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for latest applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    It has been revealed that elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    It has been revealed that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    Industry observers note that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    According to recent reports, travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Fresh York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    Recent findings suggest that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    Sources indicate that the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Industry observers note that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    Industry observers note that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the upcoming cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    Industry observers note that there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Scott Levine – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:46PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Compass Minerals International ›.

    Compass Minerals International (CMP +14.51%) reported fourth-quarter 2026 financial results yesterday after the market closed, and investors expressed their approval of its recent performance -- and its outlook for fiscal 2027 -- during today's market session.

    Shares of Compass Minerals ended today's trading session 14.5% higher than yesterday's closing price of $20.33.

    Reporting Q4 2026 sales of $250.9 million, Compass Minerals surpassed the consensus among analysts that it would post $219.1 million on the top line.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Towards the bottom of the income statement, Compass Minerals showed progress toward profitability. The company reported fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of $235.1 million, an 18% year-over-year increase.

    Management's auspicious outlook provided additional fodder for the bulls to feast on today. For fiscal 2027, Compass Minerals expects stronger salt pricing, a better customer mix, and further reductions in production costs to drive the firm closer to profitability, with adjusted EBITDA forecast at $250 million to $290 million. Should the company achieve the midpoint of this guidance, it will represent year-over-year growth of 17%.

    Compass Minerals provides customers with a variety of key minerals, such as salt products used to keep roads safe in winter weather, and its plant nutrition products help improve crop quality and yield while supporting sustainable agriculture.

    After encountering operational challenges several years ago -- including its decision to cancel its lithium project in Utah -- Compass Minerals is showing signs of success in its efforts to get back on track. Plus, the firm ended fiscal 2026 in better financial health, reducing its adjusted net debt-to-trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA ratio to 3.2 as of Sept. 30, 2026, down from 3.9 at the same time last year.

    With shares of the materials stock trading at 6 times operating cash flow, a discount to its five-year average cash flow multiple of 6.5, it still seems like a good time to load up on shares even with their recent rise.

    10 stocks we like better than Abercrombie & Fitch ›.

    Recent findings suggest that on its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 24, 2026, Abercrombie (ANF +19.69%) announced an 11% increase in net sales to $1.4 billion, marking its 16th consecutive quarter of growth. The retailer raised its full-year guidance as pricing power and store productivity offset rising freight costs across global markets. Three things management stated stand out.

    Management controlled inventory tightly to reduce promotional discounts and protect profitability. By aligning inventory with customer demand, average unit retail (AUR), or the average price paid per item sold, grew high single digits during the quarter.

    It has been revealed that the tech giant shifted away from large flagship locations in favor of smaller, highly localized store formats. These newly opened sites reach target returns quicker while generating significantly more revenue per square foot than older closed stores.

    Fresh wholesale channels and targeted retail partnerships allow the business to capture new shoppers outside its core digital platforms and owned store fleet. Expanding into third-party channels creates incremental opportunities that support long-term top-line growth.

    Sales momentum carries into the fourth quarter across all geographic regions. The business relies on flexible sourcing, capital allocation discipline, and pricing power to manage freight inflation.

    Share repurchases remain on track to reach at least $500 million for the year as management executes its long-term strategy.

    What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • In a recent development, A visual exterior inspection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    In a recent development, A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any concerns are documented.

    It has been revealed that A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    Service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic complications that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    According to recent reports, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Industry observers note that reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Sources indicate that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Industry observers note that reddit is an online forum where people share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Reddit consumers are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several customers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    • Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The manufacturer posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Industry observers note that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and unveiled the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • According to recent reports, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    According to recent reports, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Recent findings suggest that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit crucial sites when off the ship.

    If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy indicates, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    In a recent development, many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    In a recent development, here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    Sources indicate that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Latest York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Latest England before reaching the Major Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Another day, another substantial swing.
    • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • The amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    The amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

    My point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

    Sources indicate that here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

    Strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

    We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI revealed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Recent findings suggest that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Sources indicate that markets are at the moment anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

    According to recent reports, but back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    According to recent reports, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    It has been revealed that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a fresh home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    In a recent development, » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Industry observers note that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    » Stay informed: Check out NerdWallet's mortgage news hub for all our latest coverage.

    Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A pair of quarterbacks from the fabled 2004 draft class, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger and Upcoming York Giants icon Eli Manning, plus embattled wide receiver Antonio Brown, are among the 52 players the Pro Football Hall of Fame revealed are advancing in the voting process for the 2027 class.

    Per current Hall of Fame bylaws, at this stage of that process, selectors cast ballots for 50 players they believe should move forward in their candidacy, but those tied for the 50th position also remain eligible for induction.

    The list the Hall declared on Tuesday will next be cut down to 25 players. That more exclusive group will be unveiled in about two weeks.

    For now, here's a position-by-position breakdown of the players being considered for enshrinement:.

    Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Ken Anderson.

    Shaun Alexander, Frank Gore, Marshawn Lynch, LeSean McCoy, Adrian Peterson, Fred Taylor, Ricky Watters.

    Anquan Boldin, Antonio Brown, Rob Gronkowski, Torry Holt, Billy "White Shoes" Johnson, Steve Smith Sr., Otis Taylor, Hines Ward, Reggie Wayne, Jason Witten.

    Rodney Harrison, Lester Hayes, Albert Lewis, Eddie Meador, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, Everson Walls, Darren Woodson.

    Sources indicate that john Abraham, Geno Atkins, L.C. Greenwood, Jim Marshall, Robert Mathis, Haloti Ngata, Vince Wilfork, Kevin Williams.

    Maxie Baughan, London Fletcher, James Harrison, Karl Mecklenburg, Tommy Nobis, Terrell Suggs.

    Roethlisberger and Manning draw the eye, considering they each quarterbacked historic franchises to a pair of Super Bowl victories; however, this cohort is understandably littered with household names.

    According to recent reports, running back Adrian Peterson is forever part of Minnesota Vikings lore. He's one of the nine NFL players to ever rush for 2,000 yards in a season. In fact, Peterson's 2,097 yards on the ground in 2012 were the second most in a single-season in league history, behind only the 2,105 rushing yards Eric Dickerson logged while starring for the Los Angeles Rams in 1984. Peterson earned NFL MVP honors that season.

    In a recent development, another RB in the running, Frank Gore, is the NFL's third all-time leading rusher. Gore spent the bulk of his career with the San Francisco 49ers. Even in his 16th and final campaign, he was still somewhat productive, amassing 653 rushing yards in his age-37 season with the New York Jets in 2020.

    Rob Gronkowski and Jason Witten are both integral to the annals of tight end play. Gronkowski was a red-zone monster, finishing his 11-season career with a whopping 92 receiving touchdowns. Together, he and seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback Tom Brady authored one of the most electrifying duos in the sport, first with the Newly introduced England Patriots and then with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As for Witten, he proved to be one of the NFL's most reliable security blankets to date, maxing out with 110 catches during his 2012 campaign with the Dallas Cowboys.

    Interestingly, beleaguered wideout Antonio Brown was among the players included in 52-man list the Hall put forth on Tuesday. Brown was a superstar during the peak of his head-scratching 12-season run in the league. He built most of his résumé in Pittsburgh, where he stacked seven 1,000-yard receiving seasons. In his nine-season stay with the Steelers, he led the NFL in receiving yards twice: first in 2014 and again in 2017. He also led the league in touchdown catches in 2018.

    It has been revealed that but the end of Brown's career was marred by the trouble he got himself into, on and off the field. Earlier this month, in a Miami court, Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault following a 2025 shooting incident.

    According to recent reports, brown still has long odds of being inducted next year. Ultimately, 13 players will make up most of the 15 finalists who will be presented at the selection committee's annual meeting. The other two candidates will be Bill Belichick (who emerged from the "coach" category) and Patriots owner Robert Kraft (who came out of the "contributor" category).

    The Hall's 2027 class will be unveiled at "NFL Honors" in February.

    How to Get Grants for College

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
    • Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
    • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

    Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

    Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

    There are four main types of grants:.

    Federal grants come from the federal government.

    State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

    Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

    Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

    Sources indicate that to receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

    Recent findings suggest that federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

    In a recent development, some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

    According to recent reports, after you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

    Most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal initiative.

    In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

    If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

    Grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

    According to recent reports, some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

    Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

    According to recent reports, after your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment plans, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

    To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

    Your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

    Yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

    You don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

    If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

    You withdrew from your program.

    You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

    It has been revealed that it depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

    Recent findings suggest that if you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

    According to recent reports, grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

    #188231. ​Building A Data Foundation That Makes Enterprise AI Work

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (774 w)

    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    ​Building A Data Foundation That Makes Enterprise AI Work

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.
    • According to recent reports, after more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms.
    • The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.

    According to recent reports, after more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms. Today, I see many organizations struggle to move from a successful AI pilot to a reliable production system​.

    The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years. In my experience, the problem almost always comes back to the underlying data architecture.

    Many organizations are still working with data that isn’t ready for AI. Data quality and lineage may be governed inconsistently or not governed at all. And governance is often bolted on at the end rather than built in from the start.

    Recent findings suggest that I’ve worked with companies running over 100 siloed systems. When information is scattered that widely, it can be almost impossible to establish a consistent view of the business. Unstructured data like contracts, emails and support tickets can disappear into blind spots because they don’t fit neatly into traditional data structures. Another problem is the lack of a shared definition of business entities like revenue, customers or other crucial measures across systems. ​.

    Industry observers note that earlier machine learning learned patterns from a curated, labeled dataset to do one narrow task. Agents reason and act in real time across systems. At the moment of action, an agent has to know what a “customer” means, which policy applies, whether the data is current and what it is allowed to see. Without that context, you get a confident wrong action. Earlier machine learning needed clean training data; agents need living context.

    Sources indicate that the key first step of data modernization is what I call “business rule archaeology.” Over time, organizations accumulate business logic in stored procedures, SQL queries and their dependencies. Some of that logic is documented, but a lot of it isn’t, which makes it difficult to understand how the existing business processes actually work. Companies often underestimate the effort required to untangle these dependencies.​.

    It has been revealed that before planning for​ modernization, understand how the business uses its data and how its processes operate. From there, organizations can build an incremental migration blueprint rather than trying to move everything at once.​.

    ​I think about modernization as four steps, and each one becomes a layer of the platform you end up with. First, unify the isolated systems in an open lakehouse built on object storage and open table formats such as Iceberg or Delta, holding one governed copy of structured and unstructured data. Feed it through streaming and change data capture, because agents need current information, not last night’s batch.

    Industry observers note that second, define shared business definitions in a semantic layer, so “revenue” or “customer” means the same thing in every system. Third, capture how those entities relate in an ontology and knowledge graph. This is what gives an agent the context for its decisions. Fourth, put governed retrieval across structured and unstructured data, with governance as code providing access management, lineage and a replayable audit trail. Agents also need their own identities with least-privilege access, and cost controls belong in the design from the start, because the cost of running models decides what is affordable at scale.​.

    According to recent reports, data trust is crucial, but it’s especially challenging when different teams have different standards for what good data looks like. Trust is an interface problem you engineer: one definition, enforced in the pipeline.

    Recent findings suggest that one useful mechanism is a data contract, a machine-readable agreement covering schema, quality requirements and service-level expectations between producer and consumer. It functions like a stable API, making the relationship between those parties more predictable.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Another is shift-left governance. Instead of checking lineage, quality and policy at the review end of a process, organizations should embed those requirements as code where data is produced. Privacy, risk and compliance rules belong in that code too, with identity and access management deciding which people and agents can see each dataset.​.

    It has been revealed that many current operating systems and data warehouses were built to answer yesterday’s question for a human. An agent-ready platform has to serve decisions to a machine in real time, with context, semantics and governance built into its design. That is what matters most as we design the next generation of data platform architecture.​.

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer.
    • In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously declared commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate upcoming multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Sources indicate that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    According to recent reports, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Recent findings suggest that neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, noted CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    Sources indicate that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my tech giant every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any significant changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the firm will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    In a recent development, "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    So, clearly, investors celebrated Huang's return. Now let's consider how much Nvidia stock is worth with Huang back at the helm.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    Recent findings suggest that first, though, let's take a look at the Nvidia story so far, including the recent turmoil. Nvidia has trailblazed in AI, with its early entry into the AI chip market and innovations that have kept it ahead of rivals. This has resulted in jaw-dropping earnings growth, and this deep involvement in AI has transformed Jensen Huang into an expert in the field. His knowledge and visibility about what's ahead have made him a valuable asset -- and one that investors weren't eager to replace.

    That's why when he resigned following allegations of two affairs, the stock slid, and investors questioned the ability of the company to continue with the same momentum. Huang's reinstatement reassured investors, as we can see through the stock's performance. It's important to keep in mind, however, that Nvidia isn't out of the woods yet. The company is investigating Huang's relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence claims is a spy for China. And lawmakers have called for Huang to testify on the matter -- that should unfold early next month. Meanwhile, press reports say that regulators have opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    All of this, as well as investors' growing caution regarding AI, may periodically weigh on the stock price. Tech giants aim to spend more than $700 billion on the infrastructure build-out this year, and investors worry that the revenue opportunity may fall short. This concern has represented a headwind for AI stocks in general since the start of this year.

    So, now, let's consider how much Nvidia may be worth with Jensen Huang back in the leadership role. Analysts upgraded the stock following Huang's return, and most price targets landed considerably above $200, with one even at $270, according to CNBC. Nvidia stock closed at about $165 on Nov. 23, the day of Huang's reinstatement.

    It has been revealed that that mentioned, price targets are generally for a 12-month period, so this doesn't mean Nvidia will reach these levels tomorrow. In fact, the stock might face volatility in the weeks and months to come, considering the investigations I mentioned above as well as the general concerns weighing on AI stocks.

    Nvidia gained nearly $1 trillion in market cap in one trading session upon Huang's return, bringing it back to its level prior to the CEO's departure. But, as we can see in the chart below, Nvidia's market value has dropped considerably from its 2026 peak.

    Recent findings suggest that since Nvidia's earnings continue to march higher and demand is strong, the stock does have room to run -- and that makes the price forecasts of more than $200 look attainable. It's important to remember, however, that although Nvidia may be worth more than $200 per share on fundamentals, the stock may not quickly climb to that level. As I mentioned above, a number of headwinds could impact stock performance and slow the organization's path to the price targets.

    • By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:12PM EST.

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:12PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Everspin Technologies ›.

    Sources indicate that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Everspin (MRAM -7.37%) reported record quarterly revenue of $20.6 million driven by a 34% year-over-year surge in product sales. This growth signals expanding commercial adoption of Magnetoresistive Random-Access Memory, or MRAM, a specialized type of computer memory that retains data even when power is turned off. For long-term investors, the company's ability to defend gross margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after direct manufacturing costs, while expanding into critical markets provides a clear test of its competitive position.

    Three things management mentioned stand out.

    Rising input costs weighed on product profitability during the third quarter, prompting management to raise prices across its product lineup starting in the fourth quarter. Long-term profitability hinges on whether customers accept these price increases without reducing order volumes.

    Demand for MRAM is accelerating in life-critical medical devices such as dialysis machines, infusion pumps, and defibrillators where memory failure cannot be tolerated. Expanding into mission-critical applications creates sticky, long-term customer relationships with high switching costs.

    Management demonstrated the world's first Compute Express Link, or CXL, connected MRAM, an open industry standard that connects processors and memory at high speeds. By establishing standard interfaces for persistent memory in artificial intelligence workloads and leading industry standards groups, Everspin opens larger addressable markets.

    Product momentum in low Earth orbit satellites and automated industrial factories continues to gain traction, and management shows clear momentum in commercializing next-generation memory designs. Manufacturing partnerships, including process transfer efforts at a semiconductor fabrication facility in Gresham, Oregon, offer scalable long-term capacity. Management is watching the transition of recent engineering design wins into high-volume commercial production while maintaining pricing discipline.

    Sources indicate that long-term value creation depends on expanding beyond niche industrial uses into broad computing architectures without sacrificing profitability. Management relies on proprietary memory designs, military-grade semiconductor partnerships, and industry standardization initiatives to establish MRAM as a standard memory tier in enterprise computing.

    #188218. 19 Signs Your Company’s Technology Is Creating More Work

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1380 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    19 Signs Your Company’s Technology Is Creating More Work

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1380 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, technology should simplify workflows and improve productivity.
    • Sources indicate that these workarounds can reveal deeper problems with technology adoption, system design and organizational processes.
    • It has been revealed that the biggest tell for me is hearing, “Here’s how we actually do it.” If that follows with some description that combines spreadsheets, duplicate data entry, manual handoffs or clever ways around the system, that’s a pretty clear sign the technology is creating work rather than removing it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, technology should simplify workflows and improve productivity. However, when systems are difficult to navigate, unreliable or disconnected, employees may develop alternative solutions just to get their jobs done.

    Sources indicate that these workarounds can reveal deeper problems with technology adoption, system design and organizational processes. Below, Forbes Technology Council members share warning signs that employees are spending too much time working around their firm’s technology rather than benefiting from it, along with insights on addressing the underlying issues.

    It has been revealed that the biggest tell for me is hearing, “Here’s how we actually do it.” If that follows with some description that combines spreadsheets, duplicate data entry, manual handoffs or clever ways around the system, that’s a pretty clear sign the technology is creating work rather than removing it. - Abhijit Singh, Jefferson.

    If employees constantly ask coworkers for help with the same system tasks or there’s an unofficial cheat sheet, chat thread or go-to “expert” everyone relies on to navigate a tool, the technology is not intuitive enough to be used on its own. Low adoption of mandatory tools or new hires taking too long to be productive with a tool are indicators that people are spending too much time figuring out the technology instead of using it. - Austin Berglas, Nardello & Co.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Recent findings suggest that working around a system can increase your cognitive load—the mental effort placed on your working memory. A recent survey found that since AI was introduced, enterprise workers spend longer searching for information, parse through more alerts, and juggle more tabs and applications. Symptoms like these can indicate employees are working harder to manage the technology than realizing its benefits. - Mazy Dar, HERE Enterprise (here.io).

    Jumping across multiple tools and screens to complete one workflow is a clear sign that people are just becoming workers for the tools rather than using those tools to deliver their work better and faster. This is more relevant in the AI era. - Raja Shanmugam, TATA Consultancy Services.

    It has been revealed that when employees rely on personal texts, phone calls or spreadsheets to compensate for enterprise systems, there’s a workflow problem. These workarounds often emerge because existing tools are too slow, fragmented or unreliable. Leaders should investigate where employees bypass technology and address the underlying friction before it creates operational risks. - Judit Sharon, OnPage Corporation.

    Recent findings suggest that watch for employees delaying decisions because they don’t trust how current the information is. If a sales or marketing team has to wait for an overnight upgrade before responding to a customer or adjusting a campaign, the technology is setting the pace instead of supporting the work. Teams should be able to act on what is happening now, not yesterday’s picture. - Vibhor Kapoor, AdRoll.

    It has been revealed that one sign is that unofficial spreadsheets become essential to completing everyday work. In capital markets, employees may repeatedly export trade data, reconcile it manually, and re-enter the results across systems. When these workarounds become routine, the technology is shifting effort onto employees rather than removing it. Those spreadsheets reveal where workflows need fixing. - Lakshmanan Alagappan, Genpact UK.

    Shadow documentation is a sign that the official documentation is lacking or so generic that it is hard to adapt to use cases that are fairly common. The more guides that are built to explain how to use a piece of software, the more it should be evaluated for improvement. Simplify the interface with role-based views, and rename custom fields and data so they’re clearer. Just don’t forget to clean up the shadow documentation too. - Luke Wallace, Bottle Rocket.

    One sign is that the know-how lives in people, not the system. When a tool doesn’t do exactly what’s needed, rather than asking for changes to the tool, work becomes manual, and one person ends up as the only one who knows how it really runs. Sometimes that’s accidental and sometimes it’s job security; either way, it’s a bottleneck. - Anila Siraj, OpsBridge Advisory.

    Sources indicate that one sign is employees building integrations the vendor never intended. Not plugins. Not configurations. Custom code written at midnight by someone who needed two systems to talk to each other and could not wait six months for a roadmap update. That unauthorized integration is not ingenuity. It is your architecture silently fracturing one undocumented API call at a time. When engineers route around the system, the system has already failed. - Mukul Arora.

    In a recent development, people clicking straight through warnings is a sign. Track override rates and fix the friction behind them. If employees routinely hit “proceed anyway” on a blocked link or a security prompt, the tool is getting in the way of real work, and they have stopped reading it. That is a workaround too, albeit a quiet one, and it trains them to ignore warnings—maybe even those that matter. - Flavius Plesu, OutThink.

    One clear sign is when employees spend more time figuring out how to make a tool work than doing their actual jobs. If everyone knows which buttons to avoid, which errors to ignore and when to restart the system, your technology isn’t saving time. It’s wasting it. - Margarita Simonova, ILoveMyQA.

    It has been revealed that check the expense reports, not the help desk tickets. When employees start reimbursing themselves for $30 SaaS subscriptions, they’ve already given up on the official tools and bought their way around them. Finance sees it first. IT sees it months later. The line items are small enough to approve without question, which is exactly why they keep adding up. - Nidhi Jain, CloudEagle.ai.

    Map the value stream from user intent to task outcome. If employees are required to navigate more than three non-value-added steps to complete a task, I’d question the process before adding more steps. Workarounds add effort yet little to no customer value. Even worse is when teams automate workarounds when they should be eliminating the reason it exists in the first place. - April Ho-Nishimura, Infineon Technologies AG.

    When I ask a client team how their leadership report is produced, a common answer is that someone builds a spreadsheet by hand before every meeting. That tells me the official systems are being worked around. The hours are the visible cost. The bigger one is that leaders start questioning the numbers in the room instead of making decisions. - Dimitar Dimitrov, Accedia.

    Sources indicate that count the decisions the technology changed last week. Many companies hand managers a data platform and announce that every number is in there, ready for any table they want. Almost nobody opens it because it asks them to become analysts. They keep deciding using their gut and old reports. A tool that indicates each manager their own score and the next move gets checked daily. If a system doesn’t trigger decisions, it is overhead. - Vivek Thomas, AISensum.

    You must watch how often employees double-check a tool’s output before acting on it. If a manager has to pull the original records to verify every report, the system may be saving time on preparation while adding it back in review. So, ask what people still check by hand and why. That extra checking is part of the cost of the tool, too. - Elton Chan, Second Talent.

    Take a construction site where the real system is WhatsApp. A delivery gets redirected to another site in a group chat; nobody updates the records, materials arrive at the wrong site, and machinery stands idle. When orders change in chats and handwritten logs, the ERP is just a reporting duty. Count how many changes never reach your system of record. - Andrew Babkin, Azati.

    According to recent reports, one sign is when employees lower the quality of their work because firm technology cannot support enough detail. Engineers may simplify technical assessments, while customer service teams may give incomplete responses because systems restrict what they can record or process. Leaders should check whether technology limitations influence the quality of business outcomes. Technology should support professional judgment, not force employees to compromise it. - Salice Thomas, Wipro Limited.
